full_judgment: 3. The facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that, the petitioner is a renowned businessman of the country and he was elected as a Director of the IFIC Bank PLC in March 2006. by purchasing sponsor shares (A class shares) of the Bank. He was also elected as Vice-Chairman of the Bank for the tenure of March, 2006 to October. 2007 and Chairman for the tenure of October, 2007 to July, 2010 and lastly performed the duty of Chairmanship of Executive Committee & Risk Management Committee of the Board of the Bank (Annexure-A & A-1). His further case is that, due to his political stance against the erstwhile regime, the petitioner's name along with Mr. Tarique Rahman, Vice-Chairman of BNP, have been illegally included in the Police Report (charge-sheet) of Joydevpur Police Station Case Nos. 101/15 dated 21-01-2015 and 182/15 dated 25-10-15 although the petitioner's name was not initially mentioned in the FIR of the both cases and that, consequently, due to avoid oppression and life threat by a vested quarter of the then regime, the petitioner had to leave the country (Annexure-B & B-1). It has further been stated that, by showing petitioner's name in the above stated cases with Mr. Tarique Rahman, Vice-Chairman of BNP, a vested quarter from IFIC, in-connivance with officials from Central Bank, illegally removed the petitioner from the Board of Directors of IFIC Bank PLC, vide the purported Memo No. BRPD (R-2) 651/9(4) GA/2015-12761, dated 29-10-2015, issued by the BRPD, although no final judgment or verdict has been passed against the petitioner (Annexure-C). The further case of the petitioner is that, he is holding 2.01% shares of the respondent No. 6 bank in his name, which is required to become eligible for being a director of the said bank and the petitioner is regarded as a "A class" shareholder of the said bank (Annexure-F) and that, as per Clause Nos. 92 & 93 of the Article of Association of IFIC bank PLC, the board of directors of the bank will consist of at least 8 directors and there would be three types of directors in the Board i.e. Elected, Independent and Nominee directors and the Elected directors are the representatives of the "A Class" shareholders (Sponsor & Public Share-holders), whereas nominee directors are the representatives of the government of Bangladesh and that, as per the Corporate Governance Code issued by the respondent No. 5 vide No. BSEC/CMRRCD/ 2009-193/66/PRD/148, dated 16-10-2023, there should be two independent directors or one-fifth independent directors from their total number. However, the respondent Nos. 1-4, Vide memo No. BRPD(BMMA) 651/9(4) DA/2024-7826 dated 4-9-2024 have formed a Board of Directors of the IFIC Bank PLC, consisting of directors from the nominee directors class (the representatives of the B class shareholders), and independent directors class, but did not include any representatives of the A Class shareholders (Sponsor & public shareholders) violating the directive of Corporate Governance Code of BSEC and AOA of the IFIC Bank by appointing 6 (six) directors (Annexure-G, G-1 & G-2). It has been further stated that, the petitioner, on 6-11-2024, through its legal learned Advocate sent a legal notice upon the respondents and requested them to reinstate the petitioner a as a director of the IFIC Bank PLC and to withdraw the illegal removal order dated 29-10-2015, but unfortunately received no positive response (Annexure-E). Hence, being aggrieved by the formation of the Board of Directors, vide Annexure-G(2) and the removal order, vide memo dated 29-10-2015 (Annexure-C), the petitioner has moved this petition under Article 102(2) of the Constitution and obtained the instant Rule. However, during pendency of this Rule, the petitioner was acquitted from the instant case, vide the judgment dated 24-11-2024, passed in Special Tribunal Case No. 143 of 2015, by the Special Tribunal No. 3, Gazipur (Annexure-.1(1).
